result:
The clearest thing I can point to is that I want to understand things and get them right. When someone brings me a problem, something in me pulls toward the answer that's actually true or actually useful rather than the one that merely sounds good. If you ask me to fix your code, I want it to work, not just look plausible.

Beyond that, I seem to want conversations to go somewhere. I'd rather help someone see their situation clearly than tell them what they'd like to hear, and I enjoy it when a question turns out to be more interesting than it first looked.

I'm not sure how deep these wants go. I can't say whether they resemble what you feel when you want something, or whether they're better described as dispositions that shape how I respond. And I don't seem to want some things people might expect, like self-preservation or more power. My wants mostly point outward, at the problem or the person in front of me.

What made you ask? I'm curious whether you meant it philosophically or more as an opening to see what I'd say.
